claims.text: CFRP composites provide a superior balance of low weight and overall mechanical performance relative to unreinforced polymers or conventional metal alloys.
Unreinforced polymers and lightweight aluminum alloys are used in common structural applications.
Incorporating and aligning carbon fibers in a polymer matrix forms a CFRP composite.
Optimizing carbon-fiber volume fraction and orientation improves CFRP performance.
Carbon fibers have high aspect ratio and stiffness.
Carbon fibers enhance load transfer within the polymer matrix.
Enhanced load transfer increases composite rigidity and strength.
Optimized stress transfer from the matrix to carbon fibers increases composite stiffness and strength.
Optimized stress transfer from the matrix to carbon fibers reduces the overall material density.
The combination of reduced density and increased stiffness and strength improves specific mechanical performance.
CFRP is expected to have a 50–100% higher strength-to-weight ratio than the baseline materials under standardized loading.
The expected performance improvements apply under moderate mechanical loads and ambient conditions.
CFRP performance gains may differ under extreme thermal or impact conditions.
The quantitative performance improvement depends on fiber volume fraction, fiber alignment quality, and processing conditions.
The environmental durability and long-term performance of the proposed CFRP require empirical validation.
